question_text: A bicycle sharing company is developing a multi-tier architecture to track the location of its bicycles during peak operating hours. The company wants to use these data points in its existing analytics platform. A solutions architect must determine the most viable multi-tier option to support this architecture. The data points must be accessible from the REST API. Which action meets these requirements for storing and retrieving location data?
option_A: Use Amazon Athena with Amazon S3.
option_B: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda.
option_C: Use Amazon QuickSight with Amazon Redshift.
option_D: Use Amazon API Gateway with Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics.
explanation_option_A: Incorrect. Amazon Athena is a query service for S3 data but does not provide a REST API endpoint for real-time location data retrieval.
explanation_option_B: Incorrect. API Gateway with Lambda can expose a REST API but Lambda alone does not provide the analytics pipeline needed for streaming location data at scale.
explanation_option_C: Incorrect. QuickSight with Redshift is a business intelligence solution and does not expose a REST API for real-time location data ingestion.
explanation_option_D: Correct. Amazon API Gateway provides the REST API layer while Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics enables real-time processing and analysis of streaming location data from bicycles during peak hours.

question_text: A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to reduce a company's storage costs. All the company's data is in the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. The company must keep all data for at least 25 years. Data from the most recent 2 years must be highly available and immediately retrievable. Which solution will meet these requirements?
option_A: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately.
option_B: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
option_C: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Activate the archiving option to ensure that data is archived in S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
option_D: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately and to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
explanation_option_A: Incorrect. Transitioning all objects immediately to Glacier Deep Archive violates the requirement that data from the most recent 2 years must be highly available and immediately retrievable.
explanation_option_B: Correct. This policy keeps data in S3 Standard for 2 years ensuring high availability and immediate retrieval then transitions objects to Glacier Deep Archive for long-term low-cost retention meeting the 25-year requirement.
explanation_option_C: Incorrect. S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archiving does not guarantee that the most recent 2 years of data remains immediately retrievable as the automated archiving decisions may move recent data to archive tiers.
explanation_option_D: Incorrect. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone which does not meet the high availability requirement for the most recent 2 years of data and increases risk of data loss.

question_text: A company operates a food delivery service. Because of recent growth, the company's order processing system is experiencing scaling problems during peak traffic hours. The current architecture includes Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that collect orders from an application. A second group of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group fulfills the orders. The order collection process occurs quickly, but the order fulfillment process can take longer. Data must not be lost because of a scaling event. A solutions architect must ensure that the order collection process and the order fulfillment process can both scale adequately during peak traffic hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?
option_A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to meet its peak workload value.
option_B: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to create additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.
option_C: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.
option_D: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on the number of messages in each queue.
explanation_option_A: Incorrect. Setting minimum capacity to peak workload values wastes resources during off-peak hours and does not decouple the processes to prevent data loss during scaling events.
explanation_option_B: Incorrect. Using SNS to create additional Auto Scaling groups on demand adds operational complexity and does not decouple order collection from order fulfillment to prevent data loss.
explanation_option_C: Incorrect. Scaling based on queue notifications is less precise than scaling based on the actual number of messages and may not respond accurately to varying workload levels.
explanation_option_D: Correct. Two SQS queues decouple order collection from order fulfillment preventing data loss during scaling events. Scaling based on message count ensures each tier scales precisely in proportion to its actual workload.

question_text: A company produces batch data that comes from different databases. The company also produces live stream data from network sensors and application APIs. The company needs to consolidate all the data into one place for business analytics. The company needs to process the incoming data and then stage the data in different Amazon S3 buckets. Teams will later run one-time queries and import the data into a business intelligence tool to show key performance indicators (KPIs). Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)
option_A: Use Amazon Athena for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
option_B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
option_C: Create custom AWS Lambda functions to move the individual records from the databases to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
option_D: Use an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the data into JSON format. Load the data into multiple Amazon OpenSearch Service clusters.
option_E: Use blueprints in AWS Lake Formation to identify the data that can be ingested into a data lake. Use AWS Glue to crawl the source, extract the data, and load the data into Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format.
explanation_option_A: Correct. Athena is serverless and queries data directly from S3 with no infrastructure to manage making it ideal for one-time queries. QuickSight is a fully managed BI service that integrates with Athena for KPI dashboards with minimal operational overhead.
explanation_option_B: Incorrect. Kinesis Data Analytics is designed for real-time stream processing not one-time queries on staged S3 data. Using it for one-time queries adds unnecessary complexity and cost.
explanation_option_C: Incorrect. Creating custom Lambda functions to move records to Redshift requires significant development and ongoing maintenance effort which increases operational overhead considerably.
explanation_option_D: Incorrect. Converting all data to JSON and loading into OpenSearch clusters adds unnecessary transformation complexity and is not suited for staged S3 analytics with one-time queries.
explanation_option_E: Correct. AWS Lake Formation with AWS Glue provides a managed serverless way to ingest consolidate and catalog data from multiple sources into S3 in an optimised Parquet format with minimal operational overhead.
